key_insight: Intern-Atlas builds a structured "methodological evolution graph" that explicitly represents how AI/ML methods emerge, adapt, and build on each other, turning fragmented paper-centric literature into agent-readable method lineage.
problem_solved: Current research infrastructure is document-centric and citation-only, so it fails to capture structured relationships between methods (provenance, variants, adaptations). This prevents AI research agents and practitioners from reliably tracing method origins, compatibility, and evolution.
method: Define a graph schema where nodes represent methods, variants, components, and evaluations, and edges encode evolutionary relations (e.g., derived-from, adapted-to, combined-with).
Automated extraction pipeline (NLP + metadata + code linking) to populate the graph from papers, repositories, and benchmarks, augmented by human-in-the-loop curation for high-fidelity relations.
Expose agent-friendly interfaces/APIs for querying, traversing, and reasoning over methodological lineages (supporting provenance queries, compatibility checks, and retrospective analyses).
impact: Provides practitioners and AI research agents with a machine-actionable view of methodological lineage, improving reproducibility, literature navigation, and faster, safer method adoption and composition in ML workflows.
visual_elements: A node-link "evolution graph" showing methods as nodes and labelled edges for relations (derive, adapt, combine).
A timeline view highlighting the emergence and branching of key methods and variants over time.
An agent-workflow diagram showing how a research agent queries the graph to select or adapt methods (input→query→recommendation→validation).
A sample method-detail card (node-popup) displaying linked papers, code, metrics, and relation badges (provenance, forks, improvements).
paper_title: Intern-Atlas: A Methodological Evolution Graph as Research Infrastructure for AI Scientists
paper_authors: Yujun Wu, Dongxu Zhang, Xinchen Li, Jinhang Xu, Yiling Duan
